_comment: ngsolve hdivdiv#6 (Navier reference for the SS square plate, and the shipped hdivdiv_2d template being ~78% low). Verified 2026-08-03 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, maxh=0.15 order=2, E=1 nu=0.3 t=1 q=1 (D=0.0915751). Navier series coefficient 0.00406235 (textbook 0.00406), w_max=0.04436089; q L^4/(64 D)=0.17062500 is 3.846x too large. Running the shipped template's own bilinear form reproduces its deficit exactly -- w_c/w_ref=0.2187, 78.1% low -- and this fixture ATTRIBUTES it to two independent multiplicative defects: the Compliance() missing the 1/(1-nu) factor of the inverse plate stiffness (0.7002 = 1-nu) and HDivDiv built with no dirichlet so the free boundary M_nn dofs silently clamp the plate (0.3124 = clamped/simply-supported). 0.7002*0.3124=0.2188. Repairing both gives 0.04437129, 0.023% from Navier. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 repairs both shipped-template defects at the pathology site -- SHIPPED_COMPLIANCE_MISSES_1_MINUS_NU and SHIPPED_OMITS_MNN_DIRICHLET both become False, so the 'shipped' run uses the full 1/(D(1-nu)) compliance and the essential M_nn Dirichlet. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 11 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 moves the shipped centre from 0.2187x to 1.0002x Navier, so it removes 'shipped_template_low_by_gt_70pct=True', 'defects_are_multiplicative=True' and 'shipped_template_within_5pct_of_navier=False' (that key now prints True), and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear.
